title: ha(dr): automate multi-AZ DR runbooks and restore drills for private-installer + helm/terraform modules
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Added automated HA/DR runbooks and restore drills for Private Installer, updated Helm chart values for multi-AZ failover, and added Terraform module for cross-AZ resource provisioning. Backwards compatible; minor operational changes to installer flags.
description:
Context: customers running Private deployments requested codified, repeatable DR procedures for multi-AZ private installs. DR runbooks existed as markdown and ad-hoc scripts across repos; drills were manual and error-prone. This PR centralizes runbooks-as-code, automates restore drills, and wires Helm + Terraform pieces so private-installer can perform controlled failover/restore tests in a repeatable CI-friendly way.

What this changes: full list in a single string: 1) Add 'ha-drill' automation folder in redwood-private-installer that contains Ansible playbooks and a drill runner (ansible/restore-drill.yml, scripts/drill-runner.sh). 2) Add a new terraform module redwood-terraform/modules/ha_multi_az to provision multi-AZ test infra (bastion, test-db replication, cross-AZ load balancer health checks). 3) Update redwood-helm-charts/private values and templates to support graceful failover targets and a 'drill' mode (templates/failover.yaml, values-ha.yaml). 4) Add quickstart and documentation in redwood-quickstarts/ha-drill with step-by-step telemetry and rollbacks. 5) Hooked CI job for nightly DR drills (pipeline stage: drill:run) with opt-in gating.

Motivation: make DR drills regular, observable, and automatable so teams can validate backups, restore sash integrity, KV cache warmup, and service-level fallbacks without manual steps. This reduces mean time to recover and ensures Dedicated/Private customers can meet contractual RTO/RPO targets.

Design notes and constraints: - Runbooks are authored as executable Ansible playbooks and idempotent scripts (no manual SSH labor). - Terraform module scoped for test infra; recommended not to use in production without review. - Helm changes are backwards compatible: 'drill.mode' defaults to 'off'. - Drill runner supports dry-run, smoke, and full-restore modes; a post-drill verification step validates traffic routing and model-serving KV states.

Checklist (what I did): - [x] Implement Ansible playbooks for restore drill + verification. - [x] Add Terraform module with example variables and outputs. - [x] Helm chart updates with templates and thorough helm-lint fixes. - [x] Add quickstart and runbook docs with annotated telemetry points. - [x] Add CI pipeline stage and nightly schedule (opt-in). - [x] Local and CI e2e testing against a small multi-AZ testbed.

Testing and validation: - Unit: linting and helm-template checks passed. - Integration: ran full drill in internal QA multi-AZ environment; recovered service in 13 minutes end-to-end (within target). - CI: initial e2e run was flaky due to timing; added retries and post-check wait logic. Nightly pipeline now stable.

Migration and rollout plan: staged rollout for Private customers: 1) opt-in internal beta with logging/telemetry only, 2) enable drill-runner via installer flag for customer test accounts, 3) enable scheduled drills once customers sign DR engagement doc.

Operational considerations: - Secrets/KMS: installer integrates with customer KMS; playbooks do not embed secrets. - Safety: drill-runner includes a safety gate (requires explicit tag and DR-ACK) to prevent accidental runs. - Observability: added drill-specific metrics and Grafana dashboard links in docs.

Related: ENG-1423 for runbook spec, OPS-87 for incident playbook alignment.
